clue.text: One to run home through W. Shakespeare's forest?

parts.note: the initial of William, given as written
the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A riddle asking who might dash back through the woods of the Bard's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is the person in charge of a hostel or residential institution, so runs it.

clue.text: See 21
One crashes into store — to steal butter?

definitions.meaning: a criminal who drives a vehicle through a shop front to loot it
cryptically, one who raids a ram, the animal that butts

explanation.definitionFit: A ram-raider smashes a car into a shop window to grab goods inside.

clue.text: With soldier brought back to attention in court

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: brought back signals that the soldier and the abbreviation for with are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A returning soldier is summoned to stand to attention before a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns GIW into WIG, which follows EAR. The definition is the verb: to earwig is to try to win someone over by private, persistent talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig someone is to curry favour or influence them by whispering, a way of courting them.

clue.text: Christian emblem shows new ideas about horned beast

indicators.note: about signals that the reshuffled letters go around the beast
new signals that the letters of ideas are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a gnu is a horned African antelope, the wildebeest

explanation.surface: A religious symbol is said to display novel thinking about a horned animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian emblem' is the Lamb of God, the Latin name heard in the Mass; the beast is the African wildebeest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lamb of God is a Christian symbol of Christ, often shown on banners and in church art.

clue.text: Greeting from superior PM

parts.note: superior quality is good quality
p.m. marks the hours after midday

explanation.surface: A top-notch salutation from the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but it is post meridiem, the hours after noon.
explanation.definitionFit: A salutation said between midday and evening.

clue.text: Face defaced with an inhabitant of Kampala?

indicators.note: defaced here means losing its face, the front letter, so the word for face is beheaded

parts.note: mug is slang for face
and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone whose face has been vandalised is seen with a person from Uganda's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defaced' drops the first letter of MUG to leave UG.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the capital of Uganda, so its residents are nationals of that country.

clue.text: Prima donna on new bed

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: An opera star reclines on a newly bought bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low, backless bed or couch.

clue.text: Developmental stage in tabloid newspaper

parts.note: the Daily Star is a British tabloid

explanation.surface: A growth phase reported in a gossip paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star is a British tabloid daily.
explanation.definitionFit: An instar is a phase between moults in the growth of an insect or other arthropod.

clue.text: Watch male in band

indicators.note: in signals that the male letter goes inside the band

parts.note: a tier is a row or band, as in tiered seating

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep an eye on a man playing in a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopwatch or other timepiece is a device that measures time elapsed.

clue.text: See 22
Being insane those years ago?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a period spent out of one's mind
an idiom for a time long past, beyond memory

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means from time immemorial, and read literally it suggests a spell out of one's mind.

clue.text: Pragmatism is shown in study

indicators.note: shown in signals that the word is goes inside the study

parts.note: a realm is a field or sphere of study

explanation.surface: A practical philosophy is presented in a scholar's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a room, but it is a field of learning, a REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing facts as they are and acting practically is the core of a realist outlook.

clue.text: Norse book returned and revised for supplement

definitions.note: the clue's singular stands for a set of additions; the answer is the plural

indicators.note: returned signals that the Norse book is read back to front

parts.note: the Edda is a collection of Old Norse poems and myths

indicators.note: revised signals that the letters of and are reordered

explanation.surface: An old Norse text is sent back and edited to produce an appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes EDDA into ADDE; 'revised' turns AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the end of a book, extra material appended to it.

clue.text: One to assist in thought where last shall be first

indicators.note: the biblical saying tells us the final letter of the thought is moved to the front

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A helper appears in a reflection on the gospel promise that the last shall be first.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the final A of IDEA to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant, especially to an official.

clue.text: Last reminder to bank available cash

indicators.note: to bank here is to hold safely, so the reminder encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder, as given to an actor
on means available, as in a dish being on
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A final notice from the bank about money in the account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to go on.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on, to endure without stopping.

clue.text: Tight one is come to cut services

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters of these words reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A thrifty person decides to trim public provision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like stingy, chiming with the surface, but it means drunk and signals the anagram of ONE IS COME.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to save money by cutting back on spending.

clue.text: Spurs nightmare a fragile defence?

parts.note: to spur is to egg on
hell is a nightmarish experience

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur's dreadful match exposes a brittle back line.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The shell is an egg's protective casing, a famously breakable one.

clue.text: Conservative on register going round

indicators.note: in a down or across entry, on places the Conservative after the register

parts.note: a rota is a roster or list of duties
Tory is the familiar name for a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is put on the duty list and sent round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory means turning about an axis, rotating.

clue.text: Cuts groove record a gender-variant person collects

indicators.note: collects means gathers up, so the person's word holds the record and the a

parts.note: trans is a short term for a transgender person
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A trans person picks up a vinyl record with a groove cut in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trepanning in engineering is cutting a circular groove or hole, as with a ring-shaped saw.

clue.text: Extended dream

definitions.meaning: to yearn or wish for something

explanation.definitionFit: Long means lengthy, and to long for something is to yearn or dream of it.

clue.text: Composer one to profit from the cuts?

definitions.meaning: Samuel ..., the American composer of the Adagio for Strings

definitions.text: one to profit from the cuts?
definitions.meaning: a hairdresser earns money from haircuts

explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Barber wrote the Adagio for Strings, and a men's hairdresser is paid for trims.

clue.text: Thespian warm and intense in performance

indicators.note: in performance suggests the letters of these words are acted out in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor's work is described as both warm and intense on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Dennis Waterman was a British actor, known for The Sweeney and Minder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis Waterman was an English television actor, so a performer of the stage and screen.

clue.text: See-saw contest enjoyed with pint?

definitions.meaning: a football cliché for a match whose fortunes swing between the two periods of play
a pint can be drunk as two half-pint measures

explanation.definitionFit: The cliché describes a match where fortunes shift between the first and second periods; whimsically, a pint is two half-pints.

clue.text: Son of Welsh man in skirt

parts.note: ap means son of in Welsh surnames
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A Welshman's son in a kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment tied round the waist over the front, like a skirt.

clue.text: Old Roman emperor crippled and heavy

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor
U/S stands for unserviceable, out of action

explanation.surface: An ancient emperor is lame and overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: US here is U/S, the services' shorthand for unserviceable, broken.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is a burdensome one, weighing heavily.

clue.text: Scotsman after pubs becomes wild fellow

indicators.note: after places the Scotsman following the pubs

parts.note: a pub is a bar, so two bars give the plural
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot goes savage after a pub crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is an uncivilised, savage person.

clue.text: Wimbledon's finalist, French bird eschews metal racket

indicators.note: finalist here is the final letter of the word Wimbledon, not a tennis player
eschews means avoids, so the metal is dropped from the bird

parts.note: oiseau is French for bird
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A tennis final goes on while a French bird squawks, avoiding a metal racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eschews' drops AU, gold, from OISEAU to leave OISE. 'racket' suggests tennis but means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, so a noise.

clue.text: Team on call close to action

indicators.note: in an across entry, on places the team after the call

parts.note: rings means calls on the phone
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team is on standby, ready to be phoned into action.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringside seat is right beside a boxing ring, close to the fight.

clue.text: Each to secure points in addition

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so each encloses the points

parts.note: all means each in scores, as in two all
S, W and E are compass points

explanation.surface: Each party agrees to settle the points as well.
explanation.definitionFit: As well means also, in addition.
